sentences.text: This large dinosaur reached a length of nine meters and stood about three meters tall, weighing roughly 2.5 tonnes.
Its mouth contained spoon-shaped teeth, a feature similar to those found in later sauropods.
The skeleton shows relatively slender limb bones and a low, elongated preacetabular process on the ilium — the hip bone that supports the leg.
A distinctive tail club was likely used for fighting other Kotasaurus or defending against predators.
A 2024 study identified four tail clubs among nearly 400 bones from at least 12 individuals of Kotasaurus.
The skull of Kotasaurus is missing except for two teeth, making the tail club one of its most complete features.
Kotasaurus was discovered in the Kota Formation of Telangana, India, and was named and described by P.M. Yadagiri in 1988.
Remains of at least 12 individual Kotasaurus have been found in this region.
The holotype specimen, which is the specific sample the species is based on, is an ilium cataloged as 21/SR/PAL.
The Geological Survey of India assembled a skeletal mount of Kotasaurus for display at the Birla Science Museum in Hyderabad.
Kotasaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, specifically from the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages, approximately between 196.5 and 183 million years ago.
It shared its habitat with the related dinosaur Barapasaurus.
It was initially debated whether Kotasaurus was a true sauropod or a basal sauropodomorph outside the Sauropoda, and the exact phylogenetic relationships of Kotasaurus remain unclear.
